extracted_claims.text: Article 43 provides two conformity assessment procedures for high-risk AI systems under Annex III: internal control based on Annex VI, or assessment of the quality management system and technical documentation by a notified body based on Annex VII, with the applicable route depending on system type and whether harmonised standards have been applied.
For high-risk AI systems listed in point 1 of Annex III (biometrics), the provider may use internal control or notified body assessment depending on whether harmonised standards were applied.

Annex VII (third-party notified body assessment) is mandatory for biometric identification systems and certain critical infrastructure AI; most other high-risk AI systems can use Annex VI self-assessment.

For high-risk AI systems covered by existing EU harmonisation legislation listed in Section A of Annex I (e.g. medical devices, machinery), providers must follow the relevant sectoral conformity assessment procedures, with notified bodies also verifying AI-specific requirements.
Substantial modifications to a high-risk AI system require a new conformity assessment, except for predetermined changes in continuously learning systems.

Under Article 46, a market surveillance authority may, by way of derogation from Article 43 and upon a duly justified request, authorise placing on the market or putting into service of specific high-risk AI systems for a limited period for exceptional reasons of public security, life/health protection, environmental protection, or protection of key industrial/infrastructural assets.

For the conformity assessment under Annex VII, the provider may generally choose any notified body, except where the high-risk AI system is intended for use by law enforcement, immigration, asylum authorities, or Union institutions/bodies/offices/agencies, in which case the relevant market surveillance authority under Article 74(8) or (9) acts as the notified body.

Annex VII section 4.5 provides that, where necessary and after other means have proven insufficient, a notified body may be granted access to the training and trained models of the AI system (including relevant parameters) upon reasoned request, subject to IP and confidentiality protections.
Article 35 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 establishes administrative rules for identification numbers and lists of notified bodies under the AI Act.
As of March 2026, the notified body ecosystem for the AI Act was still being built, with designation processes ongoing across member states and capacity considered limited.
As of April 2026, no notified bodies had been formally designated under the AI Act for medical devices/SaMD purposes.

A news blog states that high-risk AI obligations under Annex III were to fully apply from 2 August 2026, with notified bodies under the AI Act expected to begin conducting AI Act-specific conformity assessments after that date.

A different news blog states that, under a final text agreed in September 2026, the start date for Annex III high-risk obligations was moved to 2 August 2029 (from a previously reported 2 December 2027), partly because harmonised standards and notified bodies were still not ready.

A Council document (dated 2026) describes a coding system (e.g., AIP 0101, AIP 0102) used to set the scope of designation of conformity assessment bodies notified under Article 30 for Annex I AI systems.

A Commission proposal (COM(2025) 836) proposes a new Annex XIV listing categories/types of AI systems for the NANDO notified/designated organisations information system, and proposes amendments to Regulation (EU) 2018/1139 to integrate AI Act high-risk requirements, as well as rules on entry into force.
As of October 2025, the NANDO system listed 51 MDR-designated notified bodies and 19 IVDR-designated notified bodies (medical devices regime, not AI Act-specific).

The Commission publishes designated notified bodies in the NANDO information system, filterable by legislation; MDR/IVDR require published Member State summaries of annual monitoring reports on notified bodies.

Article 43(5) of the AI Act gives the European Commission power to adopt delegated acts under Article 97 to update Annex VI (internal control procedure) and Annex VII (QMS/technical documentation assessment) in light of technical progress.

Under the Cyber Resilience Act (a separate but related EU regulation), as of late June 2026 zero notified bodies had been designated in NANDO, with a target of 11 December 2026 for sufficient notified body capacity and full application from 11 December 2027.

report:
# Conformity Assessment Procedures and Notified Bodies Under the EU AI Act

## Executive Summary
The EU AI Act establishes a dual-track conformity assessment system for high-risk AI systems — internal control (Annex VI) or third-party assessment by a notified body (Annex VII) — with the applicable route depending on the system's category and use of harmonised standards ([VDE](https://www.vde.com/topics-en/artificial-intelligence/blog/conformity-assessment-high-risk-ai), [AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43)). However, the notified body ecosystem required to operationalise third-party assessments remains largely unbuilt, and sources disagree significantly on both the current state of designations and the applicable compliance deadlines.

## Key Findings

### Conformity Assessment Procedures
Article 43 provides two routes for Annex III high-risk AI systems: internal control based on Annex VI, or notified body assessment of the quality management system and technical documentation under Annex VII, with the choice depending on system type and harmonised standard application (low confidence) ([VDE](https://www.vde.com/topics-en/artificial-intelligence/blog/conformity-assessment-high-risk-ai), [DPO Consulting](https://www.dpo-consulting.com/blog/ai-conformity-assessment)). For Annex III point 1 systems (biometrics), providers may use either internal control or notified body assessment depending on harmonised standards (low confidence) ([Futurium](https://futurium.ec.europa.eu/sites/default/files/2021-10/Kop_EU%20Artificial%20Intelligence%20Act%20-%20The%20European%20Approach%20to%20AI_21092021_0.pdf)). Some industry commentary suggests Annex VII assessment is effectively mandatory for biometric identification and critical infrastructure systems, with most other high-risk systems eligible for self-assessment, though this is a low-confidence interpretation ([Quantamix Solutions](https://quantamixsolutions.com/insights/eu-ai-act-conformity-assessment)).

For high-risk AI systems already covered by existing EU sectoral legislation (e.g., medical devices, machinery), providers must follow relevant sectoral conformity assessment procedures, with notified bodies also verifying AI-specific requirements (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43)). Substantial modifications generally trigger a new conformity assessment, except for predetermined changes in continuously learning systems (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43)). Article 46 permits market surveillance authorities to authorise temporary derogations from standard conformity assessment for exceptional public security, health, or infrastructure reasons (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-46)).

### Notified Body Role and Access
Providers may generally select any notified body for Annex VII assessments, except where systems are intended for law enforcement, immigration, asylum, or EU institutional use, in which case the relevant market surveillance authority acts as the notified body (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43)). Annex VII also allows notified bodies, as a last resort, to request access to training and trained models (including parameters), subject to IP and confidentiality safeguards (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/annex-7)). The Commission retains delegated powers under Article 43(5) to update Annexes VI and VII in light of technical progress, though it is unclear whether this power has been exercised (low confidence) ([FPF](https://fpf.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/OT-comformity-assessment-under-the-eu-ai-act-WP-1.pdf)).

### Notified Body Designation Status
As of early-to-mid 2026, sources indicate the AI Act notified body ecosystem remained incomplete: one source describes ongoing designation processes with limited capacity (low confidence) ([eyreACT](https://eyreact.com/notified-bodies-ai-act)), while another states no notified bodies had been formally designated for medical devices/SaMD purposes (low confidence) ([AIAct Navigator](https://aiact-navigator.com/blog/eu-ai-act-medical-devices-mdr-ivdr-interplay-guide)). By contrast, the adjacent MDR/IVDR regime had 51 and 19 designated notified bodies respectively as of October 2025, though these are not AI Act-specific (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A52025SC1051)). Administrative frameworks for notified body designation exist on paper: Article 35 establishes rules for identification numbers and lists of notified bodies (low confidence) ([regulation-ai.eu](https://www.regulation-ai.eu/en/articles/article-35)), a 2026 Council document describes coding systems (e.g., AIP 0101) for scoping notified body designations (medium confidence) ([Council of the EU](https://data.consilium.europa.eu/doc/document/ST-7322-2026-INIT/en/pdf)), and a Commission proposal (COM(2025) 836) proposes a new Annex XIV for the NANDO system (medium confidence) ([Council of the EU](https://data.consilium.europa.eu/doc/document/ST-15708-2025-INIT/en/pdf)).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
Sources conflict sharply on the Annex III compliance deadline: one indicates 2 August 2026 (low confidence) ([MDXCRO](https://mdxcro.com/eu-ai-act-medical-devices-samd)), while another claims a September 2026 agreed text pushed this to 2 August 2029, after an earlier reported date of 2 December 2027 (low confidence) ([AI Act News Blog](https://ai-act-news-blog.example/annex-iii-deadline-update)). This represents at least two rounds of inconsistent reporting. Sources also disagree on designation status timing (March vs. April 2026) and framing (ongoing vs. zero designations) ([eyreACT](https://eyreact.com/notified-bodies-ai-act), [AIAct Navigator](https://aiact-navigator.com/blog/eu-ai-act-medical-devices-mdr-ivdr-interplay-guide)). Nearly all claims regarding deadlines and designation status are low confidence and should be treated cautiously, as they rely on undated or unverified news/blog sources.

## Knowledge Gaps
No source provides a definitive, current list of notified bodies specifically designated under the AI Act. The authoritative deadline for Annex III obligations remains unresolved. It is unclear whether COM(2025) 836 has been formally adopted or remains a proposal, and how it interacts with the Council's AIP coding document. The precise current count of AI Act-designated notified bodies, practical use of the Article 46 derogation, and the final MDR/IVDR–AI Act harmonisation timeline for medical AI devices are all unanswered.

# Conformity Assessment Procedures and Notified Bodies Under the EU AI Act

## Executive Summary
The EU AI Act establishes a dual-track conformity assessment system for high-risk AI systems — internal control (Annex VI) or third-party assessment by a notified body (Annex VII) — with the applicable route depending on the system's category and use of harmonised standards ([VDE](https://www.vde.com/topics-en/artificial-intelligence/blog/conformity-assessment-high-risk-ai), [AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43)). However, the notified body ecosystem required to operationalise third-party assessments remains largely unbuilt, and sources disagree significantly on both the current state of designations and the applicable compliance deadlines.

## Key Findings

### Conformity Assessment Procedures
Article 43 provides two routes for Annex III high-risk AI systems: internal control based on Annex VI, or notified body assessment of the quality management system and technical documentation under Annex VII, with the choice depending on system type and harmonised standard application (low confidence) ([VDE](https://www.vde.com/topics-en/artificial-intelligence/blog/conformity-assessment-high-risk-ai), [DPO Consulting](https://www.dpo-consulting.com/blog/ai-conformity-assessment)). For Annex III point 1 systems (biometrics), providers may use either internal control or notified body assessment depending on harmonised standards (low confidence) ([Futurium](https://futurium.ec.europa.eu/sites/default/files/2021-10/Kop_EU%20Artificial%20Intelligence%20Act%20-%20The%20European%20Approach%20to%20AI_21092021_0.pdf)). Some industry commentary suggests Annex VII assessment is effectively mandatory for biometric identification and critical infrastructure systems, with most other high-risk systems eligible for self-assessment, though this is a low-confidence interpretation ([Quantamix Solutions](https://quantamixsolutions.com/insights/eu-ai-act-conformity-assessment)).

For high-risk AI systems already covered by existing EU sectoral legislation (e.g., medical devices, machinery), providers must follow relevant sectoral conformity assessment procedures, with notified bodies also verifying AI-specific requirements (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43)). Substantial modifications generally trigger a new conformity assessment, except for predetermined changes in continuously learning systems (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43)). Article 46 permits market surveillance authorities to authorise temporary derogations from standard conformity assessment for exceptional public security, health, or infrastructure reasons (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-46)).

### Notified Body Role and Access
Providers may generally select any notified body for Annex VII assessments, except where systems are intended for law enforcement, immigration, asylum, or EU institutional use, in which case the relevant market surveillance authority acts as the notified body (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-43)). Annex VII also allows notified bodies, as a last resort, to request access to training and trained models (including parameters), subject to IP and confidentiality safeguards (medium confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/annex-7)). The Commission retains delegated powers under Article 43(5) to update Annexes VI and VII in light of technical progress, though it is unclear whether this power has been exercised (low confidence) ([FPF](https://fpf.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/OT-comformity-assessment-under-the-eu-ai-act-WP-1.pdf)).

### Notified Body Designation Status
As of early-to-mid 2026, sources indicate the AI Act notified body ecosystem remained incomplete: one source describes ongoing designation processes with limited capacity (low confidence) ([eyreACT](https://eyreact.com/notified-bodies-ai-act)), while another states no notified bodies had been formally designated for medical devices/SaMD purposes (low confidence) ([AIAct Navigator](https://aiact-navigator.com/blog/eu-ai-act-medical-devices-mdr-ivdr-interplay-guide)). By contrast, the adjacent MDR/IVDR regime had 51 and 19 designated notified bodies respectively as of October 2025, though these are not AI Act-specific (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A52025SC1051)). Administrative frameworks for notified body designation exist on paper: Article 35 establishes rules for identification numbers and lists of notified bodies (low confidence) ([regulation-ai.eu](https://www.regulation-ai.eu/en/articles/article-35)), a 2026 Council document describes coding systems (e.g., AIP 0101) for scoping notified body designations (medium confidence) ([Council of the EU](https://data.consilium.europa.eu/doc/document/ST-7322-2026-INIT/en/pdf)), and a Commission proposal (COM(2025) 836) proposes a new Annex XIV for the NANDO system (medium confidence) ([Council of the EU](https://data.consilium.europa.eu/doc/document/ST-15708-2025-INIT/en/pdf)).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
Sources conflict sharply on the Annex III compliance deadline: one indicates 2 August 2026 (low confidence) ([MDXCRO](https://mdxcro.com/eu-ai-act-medical-devices-samd)), while another claims a September 2026 agreed text pushed this to 2 August 2029, after an earlier reported date of 2 December 2027 (low confidence) ([AI Act News Blog](https://ai-act-news-blog.example/annex-iii-deadline-update)). This represents at least two rounds of inconsistent reporting. Sources also disagree on designation status timing (March vs. April 2026) and framing (ongoing vs. zero designations) ([eyreACT](https://eyreact.com/notified-bodies-ai-act), [AIAct Navigator](https://aiact-navigator.com/blog/eu-ai-act-medical-devices-mdr-ivdr-interplay-guide)). Nearly all claims regarding deadlines and designation status are low confidence and should be treated cautiously, as they rely on undated or unverified news/blog sources.

## Knowledge Gaps
No source provides a definitive, current list of notified bodies specifically designated under the AI Act. The authoritative deadline for Annex III obligations remains unresolved. It is unclear whether COM(2025) 836 has been formally adopted or remains a proposal, and how it interacts with the Council's AIP coding document. The precise current count of AI Act-designated notified bodies, practical use of the Article 46 derogation, and the final MDR/IVDR–AI Act harmonisation timeline for medical AI devices are all unanswered.
